title: Developing with AWS Lambda

header.html: Grant Lambda functions access to private resources in VPCs (1.2.1); configure functions with environment variables and parameters (1.2.2); handle event lifecycles and errors with destinations and dead-letter queues (1.2.3); integrate Lambda with AWS services by using code, event source mappings and destinations (1.2.4)
the official AWS Developer Associate (DVA-C03) exam guide, Task 1.2

html:
1The Lambda model

AWS Lambda runs your code in response to events without servers to manage. You pay per request and per millisecond of compute. A function has a handler, a runtime, an execution role and configuration.

2Configuration

Setting What to know
Memory 128 MB to 10,240 MB; CPU grows with memory
Timeout Up to 15 minutes
Environment variables Configuration without code change; encrypted at rest (use KMS or Secrets Manager for secrets)
Layers Shared libraries or dependencies attached to functions
Concurrency Reserved (guarantee and cap) and provisioned (pre-warmed, no cold start)
Versions and aliases Immutable versions; aliases point to versions and enable traffic shifting
/tmp Ephemeral storage, 512 MB by default, up to 10 GB
Execution role The IAM role the function uses to call AWS
Extensions Add tools (monitoring, security) that run alongside the function

[Verify live] limits change over time.

3Lambda in a VPC

By default a function runs outside your VPC and cannot reach private resources (for example an RDS database). To reach them, configure the function with VPC subnets and security groups.

Need Solution
Reach a private database Attach the function to private subnets with a security group that the database allows
Reach the internet from a VPC function A NAT gateway (or VPC endpoints for AWS services)
Many connections to RDS Use RDS Proxy to pool connections
Exam tip

. A VPC-attached Lambda loses internet access unless you add a NAT gateway or a VPC endpoint.

4Invocation types, errors and destinations

Invocation Who calls Retries
Synchronous API Gateway, SDK RequestResponse The caller handles errors
Asynchronous S3, SNS, EventBridge, SDK Event Lambda retries twice by default, then uses destinations or a DLQ
Event source mapping (polling) SQS, Kinesis, DynamoDB Streams: Lambda polls and invokes Depends on the source; failed batches retry
Error tool Purpose
Destinations Send success or failure results (with details) to SQS, SNS, EventBridge or Lambda
Dead-letter queue Send failed async events to SQS or SNS
Partial batch response For SQS/Kinesis, report only the failed items so the rest are not retried
Bisect on error / max retry Kinesis and DynamoDB Streams: split a failing batch to isolate the bad record
Exam tip

. For SQS-triggered Lambda, set the queue's visibility timeout to at least six times the function timeout [Verify live], and configure a DLQ on the queue (not on the function).

Exam tip

. Reserved concurrency guarantees and caps; provisioned concurrency removes cold starts. Do not swap them.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A Lambda function must read from a database in a private subnet. What must the developer configure?

  • AAttach the function to the VPC subnets with a suitable security group
  • BMake the database publicly accessible and use its public endpoint
  • CIncrease the function memory to 10 GB so it can reach the database
  • DAdd a Lambda layer that contains the database driver and its certificates
Show the answer

Answer: A. VPC configuration lets the function reach private resources.

S2After attaching a function to a VPC, calls to a public API time out. What is the best fix?

  • ARemove the execution role so the function uses the default network path
  • BReduce the function timeout so the call fails faster and retries
  • CUse a larger layer that contains a proxy for outbound requests
  • DAdd a NAT gateway for the function's subnets
Show the answer

Answer: D. VPC-attached functions need NAT or endpoints to reach outside the VPC.

S3An asynchronous Lambda invocation keeps failing and events are lost. Which feature keeps the failed events?

  • AA larger memory setting so the function finishes before it fails
  • BA dead-letter queue or a failure destination
  • CA new alias that points to the previous version of the function
  • DReserved concurrency of zero so that no further events are accepted
Show the answer

Answer: B. DLQs and destinations capture failed asynchronous events.

S4Which change gives a function more CPU?

  • AIncrease its memory
  • BIncrease its timeout
  • CAdd an environment variable
  • DAdd a layer
Show the answer

Answer: A. CPU is allocated in proportion to memory.

S5A function polling an SQS queue should retry only the failed messages of a batch. What should the developer use?

  • AA larger batch window so failures are spread across more messages
  • BSynchronous invocation so the queue never retries any message
  • CPartial batch response (report batch item failures)
  • DA new Region so that failed messages are processed somewhere else
Show the answer

Answer: C. Partial batch responses return only the failed items.

S6How can a team remove cold start latency for a latency-sensitive function?

  • AProvisioned concurrency
  • BA dead-letter queue
  • CA smaller timeout
  • DEnvironment variables
Show the answer

Answer: A. Provisioned concurrency keeps execution environments initialized.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What is the maximum Lambda timeout?

Show the answer

15 minutes.

R2What memory range can a function use?

Show the answer

128 MB to 10,240 MB.

R3How many times does Lambda retry an asynchronous invocation by default?

Show the answer

Twice.

R4Which event sources does Lambda poll?

Show the answer

SQS, Kinesis and DynamoDB Streams (event source mappings).

R5What is the difference between reserved and provisioned concurrency?

Show the answer

Reserved guarantees and caps concurrency; provisioned pre-warms environments.

R6What attaches shared libraries to many functions?

Show the answer

Lambda layers.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Config memory 128-10,240 MB (CPU follows), timeout 15 min, env vars, layers, aliases
VPC subnets + security groups; NAT or endpoints for outside access; RDS Proxy
Invocation sync, async (2 retries, DLQ, destinations), polling (SQS, Kinesis, DynamoDB Streams)
